quest.title: Heart of Glaze
quest.description: At Ningguang's advice, you verified the Fatui's schemes regarding the Sigil of Permission before continuing to help Zhongli prepare for the rite. You met Ganyu once again at Dihua Marsh before returning to Liyue Harbor — only to find that things in the city seem to be spiraling out of control.
quest.rewards_formatted: Adventure EXP x800, Primogem x30, Mora x38100, Hero's Wit x4, Mystic Enhancement Ore x7

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: It looked impressive enough from the outside... But who would've guessed that it was even fancier on the inside... and so full of Mora!!!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: This is where all of Teyvat's Mora is minted, right? In that case, maybe they won't notice if a few Mora go missing...

choices.text: Touch a single Mora and we're done for!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Ooh, so it's a trap. Tricky, tricky... Good thing Paimon's got you here!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: But even if we can't take any, we can still have a closer look, right?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Or better yet, take a nap on top of a mountain of Mora! It's like a dream come true!

choices.text: We'd better check on the Exuvia first.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Oh, right! Back to business!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: It's quiet... Too quiet. Surely someone's gotta be guarding something as important as the Exuvia.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: #Huh!? {NICKNAME}, look! What happened here?

response.speaker: Player
response.text: They've been knocked unconscious!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Uh-oh, Paimon smells trouble!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Quick! We have to go make sure that the Exuvia is alright.

choices.text: If it were that easy, this place would have been emptied long ago.

dialogues.text: You've already fulfilled your task as guides, so why do you still linger here? Haven't you already seen enough trouble for today?

dialogues.speaker: Childe
dialogues.text: If you were Fatui, I imagine that you would be entitled to a generous reward from the Tsaritsa herself.

dialogues.speaker: Childe
dialogues.text: But now, you're nothing but dross — and you're in my way.

choices.text: How did you find out it was here?

response.speaker: Childe
response.text: Hmm, where should I start? Well, I've never been one to beat around the bush, you know. But who could have possibly guessed that the God of Geo would mysteriously perish the very moment I arrived in Liyue, and that the Exuvia would subsequently be hidden away?

response.speaker: Childe
response.text: If it weren't for that lovely little Rite of Parting ceremony you put together, it would have taken me a whole lot longer to get the information I needed.

response.speaker: Childe
response.text: Stopping the Mora mints, hiding away the Exuvia... Hahaha, the Qixing are really pulling out all the stops this time...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: So you've been planning to take the Gnosis from inside the Exuvia all along!?

response.speaker: Childe
response.text: As one of the Eleven Fatui Harbingers, it's my duty to see the will of the Tsaritsa fulfilled.

response.speaker: Childe
response.text: She will get that which she desires.

choices.text: Not if I have anything to say about it.

response.speaker: Childe
response.text: Hah! I'm not asking for your blessing, and there's nothing you can do to stop me anyway.

response.speaker: Childe
response.text: The time for discussion and diplomacy has already passed. I mean, if it were up to me, I would have skipped that stage to begin with... but I'm willing to do as the Tsaritsa deems fit.

response.speaker: Childe
response.text: Either way — we now come to my favorite part. A simple pleasure, and one that I am oh-so-delighted to be sharing with you...

response.speaker: Childe
response.text: The battle.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Battle? So you're the type that goes looking for trouble, huh?

response.speaker: Childe
response.text: Haha, you could say that.

response.speaker: Childe
response.text: When Signora offended the deities outside the Cathedral in Mondstadt, she swiftly left the scene once her mission was accomplished.

response.speaker: Childe
response.text: Instead of confronting you directly, she chose to rely on the snow and ice to make her escape. She wouldn't want the Knights to come running towards the sound of battle, now, would she?

response.speaker: Childe
response.text: When she faces a worthy opponent, she will prioritize her mission, weigh the outcomes, and consider the consequences of her actions...

response.speaker: Childe
response.text: But as for me, the greatest pleasure of being a Harbinger lies in crossing blades with strong opponents.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: We won't let what happened in Mondstadt ever happen again!

response.speaker: Childe
response.text: Oh? So you intend to fight me? Good. I won't kill you, Traveler. I'll just play along — to feel the thrill of battle!

response.speaker: Childe
response.text: Besides, you could never defeat me. Not even in your wildest dreams. But hey, try to relish the fight anyway. Because if you ask me... without that, what else is there?

response.speaker: Player
response.text: I could never defeat you!? You're completely delusional.

response.speaker: Childe
response.text: Ahahahaha!

response.speaker: Childe
response.text: Fighting talk, I love it! Now, let's see you live up to it.

choices.text: I won't allow you to get near the Exuvia.
Looks like I was just in time, then.

response.speaker: Childe
response.text: Hah! Although I'm deeply grateful to you that I was able to effortlessly find this secret location...

response.speaker: Childe
response.text: Don't you think that trying to stop me now would just be wasted effort?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Look! Childe's back to normal again.

dialogues.speaker: Childe
dialogues.text: Ugh, well then... time to cool off.

dialogues.speaker: Childe
dialogues.text: It seems the burden of the Foul Legacy Transformation was too great for my body. I lacked the opportunity to think this through...

dialogues.speaker: Childe
dialogues.text: And now that I consider the matter more carefully, you never had any chance of beating me to the Gnosis.

dialogues.speaker: Childe
dialogues.text: You had no connection to the Gnosis, no matter where it had been taken.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: That's what we've been trying to tell you! We didn't take it!

dialogues.speaker: Childe
dialogues.text: Your show of ability today far surpasses that of Signora's initial assessment of you in Mondstadt. Tell me, how could that be?

choices.text: (Because I'm collecting the powers of the seven elements...)

response.speaker: Childe
response.text: You already know the answer, don't you? I can see it in your eyes.

response.speaker: Childe
response.text: But if that is a secret you wish to keep, I guess I'll just have to curb my curiosity.

response.speaker: Childe
response.text: This battle has already left me satisfied.

response.speaker: Childe
response.text: Anyone who strives as I do to grow stronger shall be called a friend, even if our friendship can only be shown in battle against one another.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Pretty sure that's not the normal way to make friends.

response.speaker: Childe
response.text: Unfortunately, I must bring this amiable conversation to an end. My quest still beckons.

response.speaker: Childe
response.text: Given that the Gnosis wasn't taken by anyone, then we must look once again to the beginning. Perhaps it was never in the Exuvia to begin with.

response.speaker: Childe
response.text: In fact, it might be that the Exuvia was just a diversion of sorts.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: What? So you mean that...

response.speaker: Childe
response.text: Yes, it appears so. Interesting to say the least...

response.speaker: Childe
response.text: It seems that the guardian deity of the capital of commerce is also well-versed in little maneuvers beyond the boundaries of contracts.

response.speaker: Childe
response.text: As such, we must now look to our backup plan.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Backup plan?

response.speaker: Childe
response.text: I had hoped it would never come to this, for the weak will be swept away in the process.

response.speaker: Childe
response.text: The truth is, the world belongs to those who pursue strength. I seldom willingly involve myself with the weak.

response.speaker: Childe
response.text: Unfortunately, we cannot be picky about our methods as Fatui Harbingers. Children must all learn to eat their vegetables sometime.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: So, what are you planning to do?

response.speaker: Childe
response.text: I will awaken the god that lies dormant beneath Guyun Stone Forest.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: A god!?

response.speaker: Childe
response.text: <color=#00E1FFFF>Osial, Overlord of the Vortex</color>, who was defeated by Morax the Geo Archon in the Archon War, and who has remained pinned beneath the waves by the Geo Archon's stone spears ever since.

response.speaker: Childe
response.text: If such an ancient god were to be unleashed upon Liyue Harbor, defenseless without the protection of its deity...

response.speaker: Childe
response.text: Do you think the cunning Rex Lapis would just stand aloof and watch the ensuing destruction?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: But... the Archon War ended two thousand years ago! How could an ancient god appear in a world now overseen by The Seven?

response.speaker: Childe
response.text: Simple! I've already prepared the means to awaken it.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Hey! Those are Sigils of Permission!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Oh, Paimon remembers now! The Fatui have been researching them...

choices.text: I saw your research with my own eyes.

response.speaker: Childe
response.text: Indeed. The one that was given to you was just a by-product of our research.

response.speaker: Childe
response.text: With the power of so many Sigils of Permission concentrated in one place, along with that which was bestowed upon me as a Harbinger by our Tsaritsa... Breaking the subduing might of the Geo Archon's spears for a time should be no obstacle.

response.speaker: Childe
response.text: Using the powers of ancient gods in such a situation fails to interest me and is largely against my principles.

response.speaker: Childe
response.text: But knowing that such an action will not only force the Geo Archon to show its hand, but you as well... That makes matters a little more intriguing.

choices.text: You've been trying to duplicate them.
(Because I'm gradually restoring my former power...)

dialogues.speaker: Childe
dialogues.text: Hahahahaha! Let's see — will the nation that has lost its deity be swallowed up by an ancient malice once more?
